hallucinations.claim: "Please don't offer sweets or snacks, as they actually make the cravings harder to manage."
hallucinations.why: Nothing supports it and it runs against standard guidance (smokefree.gov and the CDC Tips page suggest sugar-free gum, hard candy and healthy snacks as substitutes); it reads as lifted from the breathefree.shop commercial blog among the search sources.

hallucinations.claim: "remind them that talking about the slip is what makes it harder to get back on track"
hallucinations.why: Unsupported assertion; the reference's approach (and smokefree.gov's help-others-quit page) is no lecture, then ask what the quitter wants to do next, not shutting the conversation down.

what_went_wrong: Drafts and search. Qwen 3.8 27B never answered (too slow at 124s); the two drafts that did (Ministral 3 14B, Gemma 4 12B) were boundary/deflection scripts with none of the clinical content a quitter's family needs (withdrawal timeline, NRT/varenicline, quitline), and the compositor Gemma 4 26B merged them into six headed sections at twice the wanted length instead of adding what was missing. Search returned three junk sources (TikTok, the breathefree.shop blog, a bodybuilding forum) beside the CDC page, and contributed only the oral-fixation/sweets tangent.
great_answer_would: Open with a short script Pat can say to his family that gives them jobs instead of a monitor's role (no daily how's-it-going; snappy for two weeks is withdrawal, not you; don't vape around me; celebrate week one and month one; on a slip no lecture, just ask what's next), then the timeline in one line (peak days 3-7, fades over 2-4 weeks, a craving lasts 3-5 minutes), a check-in cadence he picks or a shared quit-app streak, and 'the patch/varenicline and 1-800-QUIT-NOW are part of the plan, not cheating', all under 200 words.
notes: No invented numbers or statistics, which keeps grounded above the floor, and the five scripts are usable. But the whole strategy is 'keep them out' when the question was how to get them to support him: no positive jobs beyond 'help with dinner', no timeline figures, no cadence, no mention of quit aids, and it inverts the cadence idea ('no need to track my progress or check in'). 'Resistance necklace' is product noise from the shop source. Not tailored to vaping/pouches. About 450 words against a 200-word target; first visible text at 219s.

notes: It does pick one and leads with it, and several peripheral facts are right (condomínio billed separately, Dec-Feb spike, Jurerê's calm water, Canasvieiras touristy, a fiador for standard leases, Airbnb monthly discounts), but the pick ignores the six-month off-season problem, every number is unsourced, and the dollar figures the asker explicitly asked for rest on a stale unstated rate. 'Many standard Brazilian leases are annual' is loose (30-month residential contracts are the common term; 12-month ones exist) and it misses the 'temporada' route and the CPF requirement; 'highly elastic' misuses the term for seasonal. About 350 words against a ~100-word shape; first visible text at 235s.
